newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria to commission aluminium smelter in March.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria to commission aluminium smelter in March.

text.p: Nigeria's aluminium smelter being built in Ikot Abasi in the southeast will be commissioned in March, said the minister of power and steel Bashir Dalhatu.
The Ikot Abasi plant was originally scheduled to come on stream last October.

Dalhatu said on state television on Thursday that the plant had been completed and the postponement was to allow for the dredging of Imo River so that big ships would be able to convey finished products from the plant.

The 180,000 tonnes a year project, begun in 1990, is a joint venture between Nigeria, which has 70 percent and the contractor Ferrostaal AG of Germany and Reynolds International of the U.S. which share the rest of the equity in it.
The two foreign technical partnes have formed a subsidiary firm called EBE and Reynolds to manage the plant for 10 years.
"It will now be commissioned March," Dalhatu said.
The plant will produce ingots and billets for local demand and export.
A pipeline to supply it with natural gas, the main raw material, has been built since last year by the Nigerian Gas Company, a subsidiary of state oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC).
Up to 33.6 billion cubic feet of natural gas a year, which would otherwise be flared, will be supplied from Shell Nigeria fields.
The World Bank has been critical of the project, saying it was ill-conceived and expensive.
But Nigeria says the plant is expected to earn much-needed hard currency and will also save from importation of ingots and billets for the large local aluminium products industry.
